title: Ops weekly snapshot — heatmap & regional capacity insights
content:
Weekly ops snapshot for the infrastructure team (focused on fleet heatmap signals and regional capacity priming). This is an intentionally concise, action-oriented standup digest — notes collected during the 07/22 regional ops huddle and followups from the priming experiment retrospective.

Attendees: Aisha (note-taker), Marcus, Priya, Diego, Naomi, SRE oncall (Ken), Capacity PM (Lena)

High-level summary:
- Fleet-wide utilization: baseline 62% (7d avg). Stable in us-west and eu-west, emerging surge patterns in southeast-asia.
- Heatmap takeaway: southeast-asia shows concentrated cold-start blocks (spike in 95th pct tail for first-token latencies during 00:00–06:00 UTC).
- Prewarming experiment 3: delivered measurable drop in cold-start tail in us-west but limited improvement in APAC due to instance spinup policy mismatch.
- Short-term ask: roll a targeted prewarm policy for APAC edge pools with staggered life-cycling; validate over next 72h.

Metrics snapshot (approx):
- 7d token throughput: 8.9B tokens/day
- Avg token latency (hosted): 120ms (p50), 740ms (p95)
- Cold-start rate (requests that hit unprimed nodes): 3.2% global, 6.8% SE-Asia region
- GPU spare capacity buffer (global): 9% (target 10%)

Heatmap & regional observations:
- SE-Asia night-window: traffic is bursty due to regionally scheduled batch jobs from a partner; these show high variance in sequence length (1–8k tokens) and cause KV cache churn.
- us-west: prefix-caching benefiting long-tail conversational workloads; lower cold-start incidence after recent allocator tweak.
- eu-central: sustained higher memory pressure on a small subset of nodes; appears correlated with an older quantized model variant (v2-q4f) still routed for A/B tests.
- Edge pools with prewarming enabled show a 45–60% reduction in first-token p95 but still a persistent 10–15% residual tail due to kernel load/unload costs on heterogenous hardware.

Decisions made during huddle:
- Ramp APAC staggered prewarm pilot (3x smaller footprint initially) to test policy stability and cost impact (approve: Lena + Ops).
- Temporarily pin traffic in eu-central away from v2-q4f for the next 48h while we investigate memory hot-paths (action: Diego).
- Increase global spare buffer to 11% for the next 2 weeks to hedge expected partner batch window next month (owner: Marcus).

Experiment notes / learnings:
- Prewarming variant B (staggered lifecycling + lightweight cache snapshot) reduced cold-starts but increased steady-state allocation churn; need to tune TTLs.
- Snapshot sizes matter: >120MB snapshot has diminishing returns on p95 due to snapshot restore time; target ~64–96MB for balance.
- Autoscaler threshold hysteresis helped reduce oscillation in us-west but had negligible effect in SE-Asia where demand is asynchronous.

Risks & open questions:
- Partner batch jobs in SE-Asia could increase load by 2–3x during scheduled windows — need clearer SLOs and contact with partner to coordinate.
- Rolling pinning in eu-central may reveal more regressions; ensure quick rollback path for A/B test routing.
- If we increase spare buffer, cost delta needs signoff from Capacity PM before long-term adoption.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Aisha: Deploy APAC staggered prewarm pilot config to canary pool and monitor 2x/day dashboards — ETA: 2029-07-23 EOD.
- Diego: Investigate v2-q4f memory hot-paths and produce reproducer (add logs / flamegraphs) — ETA: 2029-07-24.
- Marcus: Adjust global buffer to 11% and publish cost delta estimate to #capacity (include hourly burn estimate) — ETA: 2029-07-23 morning.
- Priya: Add partner batch job owners to oncall rotation calendar + request runbook for scheduled batch windows — ETA: 2029-07-26.
- Naomi / SRE: Validate rollback play for eu-central pin (test route revert, health checks) — ETA: 2029-07-23.

Short playbook snippet (for oncall):
- If cold-start p95 > 1.5s in a region for 15m: triage heatmap -> identify unprimed host groups -> trigger immediate prewarm snapshot restore (runbook: /runbooks/prewarm-restore).
- If memory pressure spike detected on a node class: cordon nodes, route traffic off, collect heap/profile, restart instance with updated kernel flag.
- For partner-induced surges: enable temporary rate-limiter for batch routes and engage partner point-of-contact.

Notes to self / unfinished ideas:
- Explore incremental snapshot diffing to reduce restore size for large model states. Could be especially helpful for heterogeneous fleets.
- Consider a lightweight in-memory cache bootstrap (no disk snapshot) for <32MB state to speed restores on smaller models.
- Add a small 'burst-only' pool in SE-Asia that is isolated from conversational traffic to absorb partner batch spikes. Cost model first.

Meeting attachments & links:
- priming sim results: GITHUB:infra/priming-sim#42
- heatmap board: https://confluence.redwood.example/edge-heatmap
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1147 (APAC prewarm pilot)

Next checkin: quick sync Monday 07/25 — status updates in thread; escalate any >20% deviation from baseline metrics.

End of snapshot.
